Priya Kaur: hey team — hitting something weird with embeddings endpoint. sending a single string but responses sometimes have length 0 or "dimension mismatch" error. started after we switched client lib to an internal wrapper. low traffic (1-2 req/s) but latency spikes. pasted payload below. any ideas? :confused:

Alex M: thanks — can you paste the exact curl (or SDK call) you used + the raw response body? helps to see the JSON shapes.

Priya Kaur: here's the curl i used (trimmed):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":"search term"}'
```

response (400):

```
{"error":{"message":"Invalid input shape: expected list of strings, got string","code":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

Priya Kaur: but sometimes it returns something like:

```
{"data":[{"embedding":[],"index":0}]}
```

Priya Kaur: other times when i wrap input in an array it works: `-d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["search term"]}'` — but our wrapper was supposed to add that array automatically for single inputs.

Javier R: interesting. two things to watch: 1) some client wrappers accidentally double-wrap, e.g., `[["text"]]` which becomes nested list-of-list and trips schema validation or produces empty embeddings depending on downstream logic; 2) sometimes JSON encoding via our internal envelope adds a string-escaped JSON blob, turning the payload into `{"input":"[\"search term\"]"}` (input is a string containing JSON) — that would also cause shape errors.

Maya L: i pulled logs for Priya's api key around that timestamp. seeing alternating 400s with message `Invalid input shape` and 200s where embedding array length is 0. stack traces point to our tokenizer returning empty tokens for weird payload shapes, then runtime returns empty embedding vector rather than error for a specific model variant (ugly edge case we recently patched but not fully rolled out).

Alex M: can you repro locally with the wrapper? if you can post the wrapper's code that serializes the payload we can quickly check for double-wrapping or stringified JSON.

Priya Kaur: here's the wrapper snippet (JS, minimal):

```
function preparePayload(input) {
  // input may be string or [string]
  if (Array.isArray(input)) {
    return { model: 'open-embed-1536', input: input };
  }
  // ensure single input becomes a list
  return { model: 'open-embed-1536', input: [input] };
}

// calling code
const payload = preparePayload(userInput);
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify({ envelope: payload }) });
```

Priya Kaur: oh. i think i see the problem — our fetch is JSON.stringify-ing an envelope key rather than sending payload at the root. our API expects `{"model":"..","input":[..]}` but we send `{"envelope":{...}}`. 😬

Javier R: yup — that matches the logs. when server receives unknown root keys we route to a permissive parser that tries to find `input` inside body; in some code paths it extracts a stringified inner object and treats it as raw input (so `input` becomes a string like `{"model":"...","input":["x"]}`) which triggers tokenizer confusion and sometimes empty embeddings. that's the "stringified JSON inside input" bug i mentioned.

Maya L: repro steps i used: 1) POST {"envelope": {"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["hi"]}} -> server returned 200 with embedding [] for variant v1.2.3 (broken). 2) same payload -> 400 invalid shape on variant v1.2.7 (more strict). shows inconsistent behavior across rollout.

Alex M: mitigation: ensure clients send canonical payload (no extra envelope). we'll patch the permissive parser so it errors consistently instead of returning empty embeddings, but that's a rollout change.

Javier R: short repro you can run locally (curl) to see the bad behavior quickly:

```
# malformed envelope -> sometimes empty embedding
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"envelope":{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["test"]}}'
```

# correct form -> works
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536","input":["test"]}'
```

Javier R: also watch out for client-side batching: if your wrapper tries to batch multiple single calls by concatenating strings into one `input` value like `["a","b"]` but accidentally ends up sending `"[\"a\",\"b\"]"` (a string) the server will treat that as single input containing brackets and return an embedding for that whole string — not what you intended.

Priya Kaur: thanks — that explains our intermittent dimension mismatch and throughput weirdness. our wrapper was doing envelope + sometimes double stringifying when the input came from a form value.

Maya L: action items: 1) Priya's team: hotfix wrapper to send canonical payload (sample fix below). 2) Support/Runtime: push PR to make permissive parser return a 400 for these cases (will avoid silent empty embeddings). 3) Rollback note: if you see empty embeddings in prod, disable affected variant until parser patch is in.

Alex M: sample fix (JS):

```
// correct serialization
const payload = { model: 'open-embed-1536', input: Array.isArray(userInput) ? userInput : [userInput] };
fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body: JSON.stringify(payload) });
```

Priya Kaur: patched wrapper and verified locally. repeated 50 requests, all return 1536-length vectors now. latency normal. nice. :tada:

IncBot: Ticket #23456 marked as "investigating" -> "fix provided by customer". Agent: Alex M.

Javier R: follow-up note — we'll add a quick SDK helper in next release to normalize input shapes and harden against double-stringify. also adding a unit test for nested-array detection.

Priya Kaur: awesome. thanks everyone for the quick triage. closing on our end.

Alex M: thanks for the fast repro and patching, Priya. marking resolved from support side. :white_check_mark:
